name: libsodium
reason: No number against a named baseline anywhere reachable. README.markdown has no benchmarks; libsodium-doc says only that primitives are 'faster across-the-board than most implementations', that crypto_generichash (BLAKE2b) is 'faster than MD5 and SHA-1', and that ChaCha20 is 'around three times as fast' as AES on platforms without AES hardware (algorithm-level, no methodology). ChangeLog speedups (SHA-2 20% faster, AVX2 ChaCha20 2x SSE2) compare libsodium against its own earlier versions. download.libsodium.org and lib25519.cr.yp.to (cycle tables against OpenSSL) were blocked. Lead: lib25519 speed tables and eBACS/SUPERCOP for a libsodium-versus-OpenSSL row once those hosts are reachable.

name: libtomcrypt
reason: Only a directional claim: doc/crypt.tex says cycles-per-byte timings are 'comparable (and often favourable) to other libraries such as OpenSSL and Crypto++', with no numbers, versions or hardware. The changes file lists only self-versus-self speedups (Shamir's trick 1.34x to 1.40x faster ECC verification, GCM table creation 12.7x, ECC projective points 3.21x to 4.53x). No third-party shootout including libtomcrypt was reachable (libtom.net blocked; FFmpeg's crypto_bench includes it but results not found).

name: libU
listed_description: Small library of basic utilities, including memory allocation, string manipulation and logging.
reason: No performance claims or benchmark numbers in the repository page or its doc directory (doxygen and man pages only); koanlogic.com blocked. Last commit 2020-12-21 (a typo-fix merge), 461 stars, BSD licence.

name: libunistring
reason: No benchmark where libunistring is the faster library. gnu.org was blocked. The only snippets found (WebSearch, pages not opened) say its speed is similar to utf8proc and that ICU normalisation is faster than libunistring and utf8proc; the utf8proc issue #12 that was opened only requests benchmarks and holds no numbers.

name: liburcu
listed_description: Data synchronization library, which scales linearly with the number of cores.
reason: Repository (README, doc/rcu-api.md, doc/cds-api.md, ChangeLog) carries no benchmark results, only the benchmark programs in tests/benchmark (test_rwlock.c, test_urcu.c, test_urcu_hash.c and others) and the make short_bench and long_bench targets. The real evidence is the paper 'User-Level Implementations of Read-Copy Update' (Desnoyers, McKenney, Stern, Dagenais, Walpole, IEEE TPDS 23(2), 2012), whose abstract says RCU read-side primitives are an order of magnitude faster than uncontended locking, but efficios.com, dorsal.polymtl.ca, lttng.org, lwn.net and liburcu.org were all blocked and no GitHub copy was found (snippet only). Lead: retry paper access; likely tier B with reader-scalability numbers against pthread rwlock.
